**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Use relay-scoped settings when building the relay DSN**

When `APP_ENV=production` and the relay is configured with only its declared `POSTGRES_RELAY_PASSWORD`, `_main_async` validates relay settings but this helper then calls `get_settings()`, which defaults to the `api` role and requires the project-planning and asset-service passwords plus the identity public key. That raises before the relay engine is created, leaving outbox events undelivered; build the DSN from relay-scoped settings instead.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Scope organization references to their tenant**

If a project-create request supplies a known organization UUID belonging to another tenant, this foreign key checks only `organization_id`; the project's `tenant_id` is independent, so PostgreSQL accepts the cross-tenant ownership link. Qualify the reference with `tenant_id` (or enforce the same invariant with an authoritative database-backed check) so the ownership chain cannot cross tenants.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Include organization_id in project idempotency comparisons**

When a request reuses an existing `entity_id` with a different `organization_id`, the existing-request path still compares only the project name and tier, so it returns the old project as if the new request matched. Since this field changes project ownership, include it in the idempotency comparison so a mismatched retry returns a conflict instead of silently retaining the old organization.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Restrict relay updates to delivery metadata**

For any relay database connection, this table-level `UPDATE` grant permits changing `payload`, `event_type`, and other event data, not just delivery state; the relay can therefore rewrite supposedly immutable audit events. The same broad grant is also applied to each partition, so restrict updates on both parent and partitions to the delivery metadata columns the consumer actually changes.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Revoke domain grants before dropping roles**

If an operator downgrades this migration after it has run, the domain roles still have grants on schema objects and default privileges created by `_grant_business_schema`; PostgreSQL refuses to drop roles that remain referenced by those privileges, so the downgrade aborts here. Revoke the object and default-privilege grants (or otherwise remove the role dependencies) before dropping the roles.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Create roles using the configured database usernames**

If a deployment overrides `POSTGRES_RELAY_USER`, the DSN builder and partition-grant migration use that configured name, but this migration creates only `outbox_relay_role`; the later grant then fails because the configured role does not exist, and the relay cannot connect as configured. The domain-role migration has the same mismatch with its configured usernames; use those settings consistently when creating and granting roles, or make the usernames non-configurable.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Use process-scoped settings for the maintenance DSN**

When `APP_ENV=production` runs the maintenance CLI with only the `outbox_maintenance` secrets and no `PROCESS_ROLE` override, `_run()` validates the maintenance settings here, but `run_once()` calls `build_migration_url()`, which loads default `api` settings via `get_settings()` and requires the domain database passwords and `IDENTITY_PUBLIC_KEY_PEM`. Even the documented dry-run then returns an error before connecting. Build the migration DSN from the maintenance-scoped settings instead.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Apply tenant RLS to the organizations table**

When project-planning code queries `OrganizationModel` through a tenant-scoped UOW, `app.current_tenant_id` does not filter this table: the migration creates it with a `tenant_id` column but never enables RLS or adds a tenant policy. The later role migration grants `project_planning_role` access to all tables in this schema, so such a query can return organizations from other tenants; apply the same tenant policy used for the other project-planning tables.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Remove app_role's outbox access**

On a clean production migration with the new API secrets and no `POSTGRES_APP_PASSWORD`, the earlier app-role migration can still create `app_role` with the checked-in `app_dev_password`: the API settings no longer require or reject that password. This cleanup revokes the role from the business and auth schemas but leaves its prior outbox grants intact, so a network-reachable database client can log in with the known credential and read or modify tenant events through the parent table. Revoke its outbox access or ensure the role cannot be created with the default password.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Enforce organization scope for project actions**

When a caller has an allowed role and a capability such as `Project:*` (which this matcher accepts), authorization does not check `definition.scope` or the requested project. The project read and status-change routes then fetch projects under tenant-only RLS, so a caller can read or change another organization’s projects within the same tenant. Validate the requested organization/project scope before allowing these actions.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Count HTTP failure statuses in the load-test error rate**

When the endpoint returns an HTTP 4xx or 5xx response, this code still records the latency but does not increment `errors`; the report labels those responses as successful, can show zero errors, and exits 0. That makes the documented error-rate acceptance measurement misleading. Count non-success HTTP statuses as failures while retaining the status-code distribution.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject the relay development password in the migration**

If production migrations run with the required API secrets but without `POSTGRES_RELAY_PASSWORD`, `get_settings()` uses the default API process role, which does not reject `relay_dev_password`; this check only rejects an empty value, so the migration creates `outbox_relay_role` with a known password. The relay entrypoint’s later validation does not prevent direct database login, and this role can read outbox events. Reject the development default or fail when the relay secret is absent before creating the role.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject development defaults when creating domain roles**

When production migrations run without `POSTGRES_PROJECT_PLANNING_PASSWORD` or `POSTGRES_ASSET_SERVICE_PASSWORD`, `get_settings()` supplies the checked-in nonempty development defaults, and this guard accepts them because it rejects only empty values. The migration can then create login roles with known passwords and grant them business-schema DML; require explicit production secrets or reject these defaults before creating either role.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Remove the unused database secret from identity requirements**

When the production identity worker is configured with its signing keys but no `POSTGRES_APP_PASSWORD`, `get_process_settings("identity")` rejects startup before the JWKS app loads. `workers/identity/app.py` only loads signing keys and serves JWKS; it does not connect to the database, so requiring this unused secret can prevent the identity endpoint from starting and unnecessarily distributes an app database credential to the key-bearing process.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Probe both domain pools for readiness**

After the connection-pool split, this alias points only to the project-planning sessionmaker, while `/readyz` in `apps/api/main.py` probes only `app.state.sessionmaker`. If the asset-service credentials or role permissions are invalid while project-planning still connects, readiness returns 200 even though asset routes will fail when they use the asset-service pool; probe both pools before reporting the API ready.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reset existing roles to least privilege**

If a deployment already has a role under a configured domain-role name with `SUPERUSER`, `BYPASSRLS`, or `NOLOGIN`, this branch changes only its password and preserves those attributes. The resulting role can bypass RLS or fail to provide the intended isolation; enforce the required `LOGIN`, `NOSUPERUSER`, and `NOBYPASSRLS` attributes for existing roles too (and do the same in the relay role migration).

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
